title: Two Indian Men Jailed in Singapore After Swapping $235,000 Diamond With Fake Stone at Chinatown Jeweller
excerpt: The pair posed as customers, replaced the diamond with a counterfeit during inspection, and were arrested at Changi Airport hours later while trying to flee the country.
body:
• Two Indian nationals, aged 30 and 42, were arrested at Singapore's Changi Airport on June 19 after allegedly stealing a diamond worth over S$235,000 from a Chinatown jewellery store
  • The men posed as interested buyers, swapped the real diamond with a fake during inspection, and left without purchasing anything
  • Police identified them within hours using CCTV and police camera footage, intercepting them at Terminal 3 before they could board a flight
  • If convicted of theft in dwelling, each man faces up to seven years in prison and a fine

Two Indian men have been arrested and charged in Singapore after allegedly stealing a diamond valued at more than S$235,000 (approximately ₹1.54 crore) from a jewellery store in the Chinatown district, replacing it with a counterfeit stone in what police described as a sleight-of-hand operation.

The Heist

According to the Singapore Police Force, the incident occurred on the afternoon of June 19 at a store on Kreta Ayer Road in Chinatown. Serasiya Milan Ramnikbhai, 30, and Mangroliya Manojkumar Kurjibhai, 41, both Indian nationals, entered the shop and expressed interest in purchasing a high-value diamond.

While examining the gem, the pair allegedly swapped it with a fake stone before leaving the store without making a purchase. The deception was discovered shortly after their departure when a shop assistant conducted a standard verification check on the returned stone and realised the substitution.

Rapid Arrest

Police received a call for assistance at approximately 3:40 p.m. that same day. Officers from the Central Police Division and Police Operations Command Centre moved quickly, identifying the two suspects through on-the-ground investigations, store CCTV footage, and police camera systems. Both men were arrested at Changi Airport Terminal 3 within hours — reportedly before they could board a flight out of the country.

The stolen diamond was recovered and seized as evidence.

Charges and Consequences

The men were formally charged on June 20 with theft in dwelling with common intention under Section 380 read with Section 34 of Singapore's Penal Code. If convicted, each faces up to seven years in prison and a potential fine.

The Singapore Police Force said it has "zero tolerance for such acts of crime" and warned luxury shop owners to "be vigilant against similar modus operandi and guard against such theft involving sleight of hand."

A Pattern of Incidents

The case is the latest in a series of theft-related arrests involving Indian nationals at Singapore retail outlets and airports. Earlier this year, two Indian women were sentenced for stealing from Changi Airport shops while transiting to Bali. In a separate incident, a 38-year-old Indian man was arrested for allegedly stealing perfumes, cosmetics, and bags worth S$5,136 from 14 retail outlets at Jewel Changi Airport.

Such incidents, while involving a tiny fraction of the millions of Indians who travel to Singapore each year, risk feeding negative stereotypes and have drawn concern from the Indian community in the city-state.
